answer: Physical token challenge registration ties each identity to a disposable microfluidic token with an imaged random pigment pattern. The enrollment rule accepts one identity per token only after its pattern matches no entry in a public atlas and rejects duplicate images. An attacker must buy, ship, and image a fresh token per identity, paying that cost; reused inlet traces are refused. The microchannel defects and pattern randomness cannot be cloned from images alone.
